plan: In a first-price sealed bid auction with independent private values, the optimal strategy is typically to bid slightly less than my true value. My value is $14, so I'll aim to bid just under that to maximize potential profit. Since I don't know other bidders' values, I'll bid around $13.5 - this gives me a chance to win while preserving some potential profit margin if I win. The goal is to win the item while paying less than my valuation.

With a private value of $34, my optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. This protects my potential profit margin. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment if I win, I want to bid high enough to have a good chance of winning, but not so high that I risk negative profit. I'll bid around $33-$34 to maximize my chances of winning while ensuring potential positive earnings.

My private value is $33. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents overpaying if I win, and ensures I win when the prize is worth more to me than others. Since values are randomly drawn, I can't predict others' valuations. Bidding exactly $33 maximizes my chance of winning at a fair price, protecting potential profit margin.
